pr_title: events: change EventTarget handler exception behavior
pr_body:
Change the behavior of EventTarget, instead of emitting 'error' on handler exception, emit 'uncaughtException'.

Fixes: #36770
pr_comments:
cc @jasnell @addaleax 

(and since this touches error handling probably also @mcollina )

> Should this be semver-major?

Hm yeah … I guess it’s possible that people have started using this, although this has only been non-experimental since 15.4.0. I’m okay with either.
Should we additionally docs-deprecate the "error" event or stop mentioning in the docs (obviously in a separate non semver-major PR) so people don't think it's the way to go in the meantime?

> Should we additionally docs-deprecate the "error" event or stop mentioning in the docs (obviously in a separate non semver-major PR) so people don't think it's the way to go in the meantime?

Likely yes

Hey, looks like since this is semver-major it needs two TSC approvals to land.

Would love some reviews on https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/37264 (the docs change discussed above with @mcollina ) :]
Adding the tsc-agenda label so that this gets more TSC eyes on it
The doc change here has a merge conflict that need to be resolved.

issue_context.title: process 'error' event is undocumented
comments:
I wonder if we want to keep it or emit uncaughtException directly since no-one actually complained about this or asked for this since EventEmitter was added.

We can also just doc it.
I was definitely caught by surprise by this being added, and would be happy to treat it as uncaught exceptions (i.e. act as if there’s no `'error'` listener present).
What's the issue here? There is documentation for this: https://nodejs.org/dist/latest-v15.x/docs/api/events.html#events_eventtarget_error_handling
https://nodejs.org/api/process.html#process_process_events is missing them – we always document events on the emitter.
@jasnell any strong opinions about making this an `uncaughtException`? I'm happy to make a PR.
About making what an `uncaughtException`? Sorry, it's not clear

@jasnell About making an exception inside a `EventTarget` event handler be treated like an uncaught exception, i.e. trigger the `uncaughtException` listener if there is one and otherwise exit the process with error code 1.
I'll try taking a stab at this

review_comments: Do we need the same stack trace enhancing machinery used in `events.js` here?
I suspect we need (in a future PR) something like `captureRejections` from EventEmitter if there is no `error` between the async function throwing and `uncaughtException`.
( and then possibly to remove the `async` behaviour entirely)
